mainTopic: Whether parts of an offering like the fetus and placenta become פיגול along with the offering; רבי עקיבא on blemished animals and a female עולה; the start of a new משנה on wrong plans during שחיטה
overview: The גמרא keeps testing רבי אלעזר's view that the flesh of an offering can be pulled into פיגול. First it rejects a proof from a משנה in מעילה about burned bulls and goats, saying its mention of לינה may mean only the אימורים. Then רבה challenges the view from a ברייתא that lists parts like the fetus and placenta as things that do not become פיגול. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only means a wrong intention about those parts themselves does nothing. רבא then proves from our משנה that the fetus and placenta do become פיגול along with the offering. Next the גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא, who lets blemished animals stay on the מזבח. רבי יוחנן limits this to small eye blemishes that came after consecration, and רבי חייא בר אבא adds that a female עולה must come down. רבי זירא challenges this from the same ברייתא, and the גמרא answers by reading it as talking about אימורים. Finally a new משנה begins: a plan to leave the blood or אימורים overnight or take them out, and a list of plans to put the blood in the wrong place on the מזבח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Wrong intention about the portions affects only the portions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier rejection: if the כהן had a wrong intention about the אימורים, only the אימורים become פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he had a wrong intention about the sacrificial portions, then the sacrificial portions themselves become פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began before this section. It says a wrong intention about the אימורים makes only those אימורים פיגול, and not the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier source seemed to support רבי אלעזר, who says the flesh of burned bulls can become פיגול. This line reads that source differently: the פיגול it talks about is on the אימורים themselves. So that source gives no proof about the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: He had an intention (here, a wrong one about time)
The sacrificial portions burned on the מזבח
They became פיגול (disqualified because of a wrong intention)

phrases.english: But if he had an intention regarding the sacrificial portions –
the sacrificial portions themselves become piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began before this section
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects an earlier proof for רבי אלעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source can be talking about the פיגול of the אימורים, not of the flesh
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrong intention about the אימורים makes only the אימורים פיגול

steps.title: A משנה about burned bulls and goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מעילה: burned bulls and goats are subject to מעילה from when they are made holy, and after שחיטה they can be disqualified by a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים, and לינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: bulls that are burned and goats that are burned are subject to מעילה from the time they are made holy. Once they are slaughtered, they can become disqualified through a טבול יום, through a מחוסר כיפורים, and through being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to prove רבי אלעזר right. This step only quotes the משנה. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important word is לינה. The משנה says these offerings can become disqualified by being left overnight. The next step will ask which part of the animal this is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls whose flesh is burned outside the camp
One is liable for מעילה (using holy property for oneself)
Someone who went to the מקוה today but must wait for nightfall
Someone who still has to bring an atonement offering
Being left overnight past the proper time

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned –
one is liable for misuse of them from when they were consecrated.
Once they were slaughtered – they became able to be disqualified
through one who immersed that day, and through one lacking atonement,
and through being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source after the earlier proof was rejected
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view that the flesh of burned bulls can become פיגול

steps.title: Overnight must mean the flesh, so the flesh can become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה's לינה means the flesh. Since the flesh can be disqualified by לינה, it can also be disqualified by a wrong intention, which is פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not talking about the flesh being left overnight? So learn from it: since the flesh is disqualified by being left overnight, a wrong intention also disqualifies it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the proof from the משנה. It reads לינה as the flesh being left overnight, and links that to פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning uses a מגו: if something can be disqualified by actually being left overnight, it can also be disqualified by a wrong intention about time (to burn the אימורים after their time), which is פיגול. So if the flesh can become פסול through לינה, it can become פיגול through intention, just as רבי אלעזר says.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? Suggests a reading of the source
Since (one thing is true, another follows)
Intention (here, a disqualifying one)

phrases.english: What, is it not the flesh being left overnight –
and learn from it:
since being left overnight disqualifies it,
intention also disqualifies it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof out of the quoted משנה
steps.raayaObject: The flesh of burned bulls can become פיגול
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word לינה in the משנה, read as meaning the flesh

steps.title: No, it means the portions left overnight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה's לינה may refer to the אימורים, not the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about the sacrificial portions being left overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It says the משנה could be talking about the אימורים being left overnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the לינה is about the אימורים, then the מגו only shows that the אימורים can become פיגול. Nothing is proven about the flesh, so רבי אלעזר is not supported.

keyTerms.meaning: The sacrificial portions being left overnight

phrases.english: No; the sacrificial portions being left overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading used in the proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה in מעילה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed לינה means the flesh, but it could mean the אימורים

steps.title: The end of the משנה talks about flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: the end of the משנה talks about the flesh, so the start should be about the flesh too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part teaches: 'With all of them, one is liable for מעילה at the place of the ashes until the flesh is burned up,' this shows that the first part is about the flesh being left overnight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 4. It points to the end of the same משנה, which is clearly about the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says מעילה applies until the flesh is fully burned. Since the end of the משנה is about the flesh, it seems the whole משנה is about the flesh, so the רישא's לינה should mean the flesh too. That would bring back the proof for רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה
The first part of a משנה
The place where the ashes and the burned bulls go
Until it is burned up completely
It follows from this that...

phrases.english: But since the last part teaches:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן עַל בֵּית הַדֶּשֶׁן
phrases.english: with all of them one is liable for misuse at the place of the ashes
until the flesh is burned up –
it follows that the first part is about the flesh left overnight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא's לינה refers to the אימורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא is about the flesh, so the רישא should be about the flesh as well

steps.title: Each part of the משנה can be about something different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases need not be the same: the רישא is about the אימורים and the סיפא is about the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a real comparison? This case is as it is, and that case is as it is. The first part is about the sacrificial portions, and the last part is about the flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5. It says the two parts of the משנה can talk about different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no rule that the רישא and סיפא must be about the same part of the animal. So the רישא's לינה can mean the אימורים while the סיפא talks about the flesh. The proof for רבי אלעזר is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a real comparison? Rejects linking two cases
As it is, on its own terms

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in מעילה does not prove that the flesh of burned bulls can become פיגול. Its לינה can mean the אימורים, even though its סיפא talks about the flesh.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume every part of a משנה is about the same thing. Here the רישא is about the אימורים and the סיפא is about the flesh.

phrases.english: Is that a real comparison?!
This is as it is, and that is as it is;
the first part is the sacrificial portions, and the last part is the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the רישא and סיפא are about different things
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה is about the flesh, so the לינה in the רישא means the flesh
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is about the אימורים and the סיפא is about the flesh, so there is no proof for רבי אלעזר

steps.title: רבה quotes a list of animal parts that never become פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a ברייתא listing parts of an animal that do not make an offering פיגול and do not become פיגול, including the fetus and the placenta.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: Here are the things that do not make פיגול and do not become פיגול: the wool on lambs' heads, the hair in goats' beards, the hide, the gravy, the spices, the neck tendon, the crop, the bones, the sinews, the horns, the hooves, the fetus, the placenta, the milk of holy animals, and the eggs of doves. None of them make פיגול or become פיגול. One is not liable for them because of פיגול, נותר, or טומאה. And someone who offers them outside the עזרה is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה is setting up a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Its list includes the fetus and the placenta. In the next step he will explain why this list causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says these parts are not real 'meat' of the offering. They do not make the offering פיגול, they do not become פיגול, and the usual punishments for פיגול, נותר, and טומאה do not apply to them. The key items for the challenge are the שליל (fetus) and the שיליא (placenta).

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (usually from a משנה or ברייתא)
They make something else פיגול (through a wrong intention about them)
They themselves become פיגול
A fetus found inside a slaughtered animal
The placenta
Exempt from punishment

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the name רבא, in round brackets. The corrected name is רבה, in square brackets.

phrases.english: And these are the ones that do not make piggul and do not become piggul:
the wool on the heads of lambs,
and the hair in the beard of goats,
and the hide, and the gravy, and the spices,
phrases.notes: The spices are the bits of spice and meat that collect at the bottom of the pot.

phrases.english: and the neck tendon, and the crop, and the bones,
and the sinews, and the horns, and the hooves,
and the fetus, and the placenta,
and the milk of holy animals, and the eggs of doves.
All of them do not make piggul and do not become piggul;
phrases.notes: The word כולן, in square brackets, is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and one is not liable for them
because of piggul, leftover meat, or impurity;
and one who offers any of them outside is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge from a ברייתא about parts of the animal that are not the main flesh.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the offering can make the fetus and placenta פיגול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the fetus and placenta among things that do not become פיגול. The exact problem is spelled out in the next step.

steps.title: רבה reads the list as never פיגול, even because of the offering
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues the ברייתא means these parts cannot become פיגול even when the offering itself becomes פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it mean: they do not make the offering פיגול, and they do not become פיגול because of the offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains how he reads the ברייתא. In his reading, the fetus and placenta can never become פיגול, not even because of a wrong intention about the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways a part could become פיגול. One is through a wrong intention about the part itself. The other is through a wrong intention about the whole offering. רבה reads 'they do not become פיגול' as covering the second way too, which would go against the view that the offering makes the fetus and placenta פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Does it not mean…?' A formula that proposes a reading of a source
Because of
The offering (here, the main animal)

phrases.english: What, does it not mean they do not make the offering piggul,
and they do not become piggul because of the offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא quoted in Step 7 is a problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the fetus and placenta become פיגול because of the offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'they do not become פיגול' means not even because of the offering, then the fetus and placenta are never made פיגול by the offering.

steps.title: No, they just cannot become פיגול through an intention about themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only means these parts do not become פיגול through a wrong intention about themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means they do not make the offering פיגול, and they do not become פיגול because of an intention about themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's reading. It says the ברייתא is only talking about a wrong intention aimed at these parts themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, an intention about the fetus or placenta does nothing. But a wrong intention about the offering itself could still make them פיגול. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts that view.

keyTerms.meaning: No (the גמרא rejects the proposed reading)
Because of themselves, meaning an intention about these parts

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say these parts can never become פיגול. It only says an intention about them, by itself, does nothing.

phrases.english: No; they do not make the offering piggul,
and they do not become piggul because of themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They do not become פיגול' means not even because of the offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They do not become פיגול' only refers to an intention about the parts themselves.

steps.title: Then why does the end of the list repeat itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if the opening line means 'not because of themselves,' the repeated line at the end seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the end of the ברייתא says, 'All of them do not make פיגול and do not become פיגול.' Why do I need this too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 9. It points to the end of the ברייתא, which repeats the same line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'they do not make פיגול and do not become פיגול' twice, once at the beginning and once at the end. If the first line already covers an intention about the parts themselves, the repeat must teach something new. That would most likely be that they do not become פיגול even because of the offering, which brings back רבה's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge to the last answer)
The latter part of a ברייתא or משנה
Again, also
Why do I need it? (points out an apparently extra line)

phrases.english: If so,
that which is taught in the latter clause:
'All of them do not make piggul and do not become piggul' —
phrases.notes: This is the line from Step 7, phrase 10. The same words were already said at the start of the list.

phrases.english: why do I need this too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 9 by pointing out a repeated line in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in Step 9 that the ברייתא only means 'not because of themselves'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the opening line already teaches 'not because of themselves,' repeating the same words at the end would teach nothing. So the end must mean 'not even because of the offering.'

steps.title: Your logic would make another line extra too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a counter-question. Even the ברייתא's line 'one is not liable for פיגול' would be extra by your logic. It is there only because the ברייתא wanted to mention נותר and טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your reasoning, why does the ברייתא also need to say 'one is not liable for it because of פיגול'? That line is extra too. Rather, since the ברייתא wanted to teach about נותר and טמא, it mentioned פיגול along with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10 by pointing to another line in the same ברייתא that also looks extra. It shows that such lines can be there just to complete a list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner said a repeated line must be there to teach something new. The גמרא answers that the line about not being liable for פיגול is also unneeded, and no one thinks it teaches something new. It was said only because the ברייתא was listing נותר and טמא, and פיגול came along with them.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a counter-question that turns the questioner's logic back on him
Since he wanted to teach: a rule was mentioned only because a related rule was being taught
Sacrificial meat left past its allowed time for eating
Ritually impure; here it means eating sacrificial meat while impure
Why do I need this too?

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
'One is not liable for it because of piggul':
phrases.notes: This is another line from the same ברייתא that רבה quoted in step 7.

phrases.english: why do I need this too?
Rather, since he wanted to teach
notar and impure, he also taught piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 by showing that the questioner's own logic would make another line extra too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-question (ליטעמיך): a line can be there just to complete a list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every repeated line in a ברייתא must teach a new rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some lines are said only because a related rule is being taught next to them.

steps.title: The repeated line comes along with the rule about offering outside
steps.stepSummary: In the same way, the line 'all of these do not make פיגול and do not become פיגול' is repeated only because the ברייתא wanted to teach about offering these parts outside the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since the ברייתא wanted to teach about one who offers these parts outside the Temple, it also taught: 'and all of them do not make פיגול and do not become פיגול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the idea from step 11 to the repeated line that was the original problem in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated line does not prove that these parts never become פיגול. It was said only because it sits next to the rule about offering them outside. So the answer from step 9 still holds: these parts do not become פיגול through a wrong intention about themselves, but they can become פיגול along with the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers a sacrifice outside the Temple
They make something else פיגול
They themselves become פיגול

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's repeated line is not a new rule. So it does not contradict the view that the fetus and placenta become פיגול when the offering does.

phrases.english: Here too,
since he wanted to teach:
'one who offers up any of them outside,'
he also taught:
'and all of them do not make piggul and do not become piggul.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the idea from step 11 to the repeated line challenged in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repeated line is said only alongside a related rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The repeated line means these parts can never become פיגול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is repeated only because of the rule about offering outside; it adds no new rule about פיגול.

steps.title: רבא quotes the first part of our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says our משנה also supports this view. He first quotes the part saying that intending to eat the fetus, placenta, or eggs outside does not make the offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We have also learned this in our משנה. One who slaughters sacrificial animals intending to eat the fetus or placenta outside has not made the offering פיגול. And one who pinches doves intending to eat their eggs outside has not made it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a proof from our משנה. Here he is setting up the first half, and the proof itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the list: fetus, placenta, and eggs all appear here together. In the next line of the משנה, some of these will be missing. That difference is what רבא's proof will rest on.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: introduces support from a משנה
Fetus inside the sacrificial animal
Placenta
One who pinches: kills a bird offering by cutting the back of the neck with the fingernail
Doves (turtledoves) brought as bird offerings

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rava said: We too have learned it:
One who slaughters sacrificial animals
intending to eat the fetus or the placenta outside
has not made it piggul.
And one who pinches the doves
intending to eat their eggs outside has not made it piggul.
phrases.notes: These are eggs still inside the bird's body.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the defense is finished, רבא brings new support for the same view from our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the fetus and placenta become פיגול when the offering does, even though intention about them does not make פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: first, the line about slaughtering with intent to eat fetus, placenta, or eggs outside.

steps.title: The משנה leaves out fetus and placenta, so one is liable for them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה then says that one is not liable for פיגול, נותר, or טמא when eating milk of sacrificial animals or doves' eggs. Since fetus and placenta are missing from this list, one must be liable for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And then the משנה teaches: for the milk of sacrificial animals and the eggs of doves, one is not liable because of פיגול, נותר, or טמא. This implies that for the fetus and placenta, one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא completes his proof by comparing the two lists in the משנה and drawing an inference from what is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list named fetus, placenta, and eggs. The second list names only milk and eggs and leaves out fetus and placenta. So fetus and placenta are not like eggs: one is liable for them as פיגול. They become פיגול along with the offering, even though intention about them alone does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And then it teaches: points to a later line in the same source
The milk of sacrificial animals
But this implies: introduces an inference from what the text leaves out

steps.confusionAlert: Here חֲלֵב (spelled with צירי) means MILK, not חֵלֶב, the forbidden fat. Read it as the milk of sacrificial animals.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof: the משנה names fetus and placenta in its first list but leaves them out of the 'not liable' list. So they are liable as פיגול along with the offering.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the clearest support for the view the sugya has been defending. The fetus and placenta count as part of the offering when the whole offering becomes פיגול.

phrases.english: And then it teaches:
The milk of sacrificial animals and the eggs of doves:
one is not liable for them because of piggul,
notar, or impurity.
But the fetus and placenta: one is liable!
phrases.notes: Fetus and placenta were in the first list but are missing here. That missing spot is the whole proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲדַר תָּנֵי: חֲלֵב הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין וּבֵיצֵי תוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof that step 13 set up by comparing the משנה's two lists.
steps.raayaObject: Fetus and placenta become פיגול along with the offering, and one is liable for eating them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's second list (milk and eggs only) leaves out fetus and placenta, which implies one is liable for them.

steps.title: Conclusion: Through the offering yes, through themselves no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes from the משנה that fetus and placenta become פיגול because of the offering, but improper intent about the fetus and placenta themselves does not make פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't the only way to read it this: in one case they become פיגול because of the offering, and in the other case the intent was about themselves, so there is no פיגול? Yes, that is the conclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's proof from the משנה and confirms the distinction it has been building toward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says intent about the fetus or placenta does not make פיגול. Yet the משנה's list of things one is not liable for leaves them out, which means one can be liable for them. The only way both can be true is: they become פיגול together with the offering, but intent aimed at them alone does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not so that… (introduces the only remaining way to read the source)
Because of the offering, through the offering's own פיגול
Because of themselves, intent aimed at the fetus or placenta alone
Conclude from it, the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The fetus and placenta are dragged into פיגול by the offering's פיגול. Intent aimed only at them does not create פיגול.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not right to conclude from it:
here, they become פיגול because of the offering,
there, the intent was because of themselves, so there is no פיגול?
Conclude from it, that is so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final inference from the two parts of the משנה quoted in steps 13-14 and confirms it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fetus and placenta become פיגול through the offering's פיגול, not through intent aimed at them alone.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: רבי עקיבא allows blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה that lists blemished animals among the things taken down from the מזבח. רבי עקיבא disagrees and says they are fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: 'and blemished animals.' רבי עקיבא considers blemished animals fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה about blemished animals that were brought onto the מזבח. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted משנה lists offerings that must be taken down even after they were brought up onto the מזבח. Blemished animals are on that list. רבי עקיבא disagrees and says that once they are up, they stay up.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a blemish, which are normally unfit for a קרבן
Deems fit, considers valid

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה there:
"and blemished animals";
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the middle of a list of offerings that are taken down if they were brought up onto the מזבח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva deems fit
blemished animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion after the previous proof has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא holds that blemished animals brought onto the מזבח are fit and are not taken down.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits רבי עקיבא to small eye blemishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says רבי עקיבא only allowed a small blemish on the eye, because such a blemish does not disqualify birds. It also has to be a case where the animal was consecrated before it got the blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי עקיבא only allowed a blemish on the cornea of the eye, since such blemishes are fine in birds. And this applies only if the animal was consecrated before it got the blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא narrows רבי עקיבא's ruling so it does not cover every blemish. He sets two conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Condition one: the blemish must be a tiny one on the eye. Since that kind of blemish does not disqualify a bird offering, it is a weak disqualification. Condition two: the animal must have been consecrated while it was still whole, and only later got the blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: Small blemishes on the cornea of the eye
Birds, meaning bird offerings
Consecration, setting the animal aside as holy
Came first, preceded

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא does not say blemished animals may be offered from the start. He only says that if one was already brought up onto the מזבח, it stays there, and רבי יוחנן limits even that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Akiva deemed fit only
a blemish on the cornea of the eye,
since such blemishes are valid in birds.
And that is only when its consecration came before its blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of רבי עקיבא's ruling quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's leniency covers only small eye blemishes, and only when the animal was consecrated before it got the blemish.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees about a female עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא adds that רבי עקיבא agrees a female עולה must be taken down. It is treated like an animal whose blemish came before its consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי עקיבא agrees about a female עולה, because it is like an animal whose blemish came before it was consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The same אמורא gives a case where רבי עקיבא agrees it must be taken down. He uses the second condition from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be male, so a female animal was unfit for this offering from the very start. That makes it like a blemish that came before consecration, and in that case רבי עקיבא does not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
A female animal brought as an עולה, which must be male
Is comparable, is treated like

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's leniency needs a small blemish that came after consecration. A female עולה was unfit from the start, so it is taken down.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
And Rabbi Akiva agrees about a female burnt offering,
that it is like a case where its blemish came before its consecration.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'consecration before blemish' condition from step 17 to the case of a female עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female עולה is treated as having its flaw before consecration, so even רבי עקיבא says it is taken down from the מזבח.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא about offering the mother outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא. Offering 'these' items outside is פטור, so offering 'their mother' outside must be חייב. That case can only be a female עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects: One who offers up one of these outside the Temple is exempt. This implies that offering from their mother would make him liable. How can that happen? Only with a female burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins an objection by drawing an inference from a ברייתא and narrowing it to one case, a female עולה. This is the setup; the actual challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only animals whose flesh is burned on the מזבח are עולות. A female שלמים or חטאת is eaten, so burning its flesh outside would not make anyone חייב. So 'their mother' must be a female עולה, which is the exact case רבי חייא בר אבא just discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: One who offers a sacrifice outside the Temple
Liable (here, for offering outside)
Their mother
A female burnt offering (normally an עולה must be male)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises an objection:
One who offers up from these outside is exempt.
phrases.notes: 'These' are the items in the ברייתא from step 7, like the fetus, placenta, milk and eggs.

phrases.english: This implies: from their mother, he is liable;
And how can you find this case?
In a female burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection to רבי חייא בר אבא's statement in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר אבא's claim that רבי עקיבא agrees a female עולה must come down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא makes someone חייב for offering a female עולה outside, which suggests it counts as fit for the מזבח.

steps.title: Which תנא could hold this ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא holds a female עולה stays on the מזבח once it goes up, the ברייתא is his. If he holds it must come down, no תנא fits the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say רבי עקיבא holds that a female burnt offering, once it went up, does not come down, then this ברייתא is רבי עקיבא's. But if you say that once it went up it must come down, whose ברייתא is this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא now completes his challenge. The ברייתא needs someone who treats a female עולה as fit for the מזבח, and רבי חייא בר אבא's reading takes רבי עקיבא off the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You are only חייב for offering outside something that would be accepted on the מזבח inside. If a female עולה must be taken down even after it went up, it is not fit at all, so offering it outside should be פטור. That leaves the ברייתא with no author.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well if you say...
If it went up onto the מזבח, it is not taken down
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that Rabbi Akiva holds that a female burnt offering,
if it went up, does not come down,
then whose is this? It is Rabbi Akiva's.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אִם עָלְתָה תֵּרֵד,
phrases.english: But if you say that if it went up it must come down,
phrases.notes: This is רבי חייא בר אבא's view from the step before.

phrases.english: whose is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection set up in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר אבא's reading of רבי עקיבא (step 18)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability for offering outside requires fitness for the מזבח. If a female עולה must come down, it is unfit, so the ברייתא has no author.

steps.title: Read the ברייתא as the mother's אימורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's inference is about the אימורים of the mother, not her flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: One who offers up from these outside is exempt, but from the sacrificial portions of their mother, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא by re-reading the second half of the ברייתא as talking about the mother's אימורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female שלמים or חטאת is a valid offering, and its אימורים are burned on the מזבח. So offering them outside makes one חייב. The ברייתא then no longer needs a female עולה, and the challenge to רבי חייא בר אבא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way)
The fat parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
From the אימורים of their mother

phrases.english: Say:
One who offers up from these outside is exempt,
but from the sacrificial portions of their mother, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the inference of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Their mother' meant the mother's flesh, which works only for a female עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Their mother' means the mother's אימורים, which works for a female שלמים or חטאת.

steps.title: 'From these' must match 'their mother'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the ברייתא says 'from these,' meaning the actual items, so 'their mother' should also mean the actual animal, not just her אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches 'from these,' and their mother should be similar to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the ברייתא should be parallel. Since the first half is about the items themselves, the inferred half should be about the mother herself, not only her אימורים. So the answer in step 21 does not fit the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (introduces a challenge)
It teaches
Similar to them (parallel)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'from these',
phrases.notes: 'From these' points to the items themselves, not just their parts.

phrases.english: and their mother is similar to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading 'from the אימורים of their mother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Parallel structure: the first half is about whole items, so the inferred half must be about the whole mother.

steps.title: Read both halves as אימורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the first half as 'from their אימורים' too, so both halves are parallel and both are about אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: One who offers up from their sacrificial portions outside is exempt, but from the sacrificial portions of their mother, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the reading of the first half as well, so both halves match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first half also speaks of אימורים, so 'their mother' can be parallel and mean the mother's אימורים. The ברייתא can be about a female שלמים or חטאת, and it no longer proves anything about a female עולה. רבי חייא בר אבא's statement stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (replaces the earlier answer)
From their אימורים
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's challenge is answered by reading the ברייתא as talking about אימורים in both halves. Then it does not involve a female עולה, and רבי חייא בר אבא's view of רבי עקיבא holds.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
One who offers up from their sacrificial portions outside is exempt,
but from the sacrificial portions of their mother, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 and finishes the defense against רבי זירא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading both clauses of the ברייתא so they are parallel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the second half was about אימורים, which broke the parallel.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both halves are about אימורים, so the ברייתא never involves a female עולה.

steps.title: Slaughtering with a plan to leave the blood overnight or take it outside
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules on someone who slaughters while planning to leave the blood or אימורים until the next day, or to take them outside. רבי יהודה says the קרבן is פסול, and the חכמים say it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone slaughtered the animal planning to leave its blood or its אימורים until tomorrow, or to take them outside, רבי יהודה says it is disqualified, and the חכמים say it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a מחלוקת about a wrong plan during שחיטה. The plan is only to leave the blood or fats overnight, or to bring them outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the wrong thoughts that ruin a קרבן are about eating it or offering it at the wrong time or place. Here the person only plans to leave the parts overnight or move them out, and does not plan to offer them later. רבי יהודה still disqualifies the קרבן, while the חכמים say this kind of thought does not affect it.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
With the plan to. This describes what the person was thinking during the שחיטה.
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח
Until tomorrow, meaning left overnight
Disqualifies / declares valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with פיגול. Here the person is not planning to offer or eat the parts tomorrow. He only plans to leave them overnight or take them out, and that is why the חכמים say the קרבן stays valid.

phrases.english: MISHNAH
He slaughtered it in order to leave
its blood or its sacrificial parts until tomorrow
or to take them outside
phrases.notes: "Them" means the blood or the אימורים. "Outside" means outside the area where they belong.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda disqualifies it
and the Sages declare it valid

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שְׁחָטוֹ עַל מְנָת לְהַנִּיחַ אֶת דָּמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion about the female עולה ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A plan during שחיטה to leave the blood or אימורים overnight, or to take them outside: רבי יהודה says פסול, and the חכמים say כשר.

steps.title: Start of a list of plans to put the blood in the wrong spot on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing plans to put the blood in the wrong place: on the ramp, on a wall not above the base, above instead of below, or below instead of above. The list continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered planning to put the blood on the ramp, or on a wall that is not above the base, or to put blood that belongs high up down low, or blood that belongs down low up high, or blood that belongs...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is starting a list of wrong-place plans for putting the blood on the מזבח. The list, and the ruling for it, continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is a plan to put the blood on the wrong part of the מזבח area. Examples are the כבש (the ramp), a side with no יסוד underneath, or the wrong height. The משנה lists the cases first and gives the ruling once the list is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp going up to the מזבח
The base of the מזבח. It did not run along every side.
Blood that is meant to be put on the upper part of the מזבח
Blood that is meant to be put on the lower part of the מזבח

phrases.english: In order to place them
on top of the ramp
not opposite the base
or to put those meant to be placed above, below
phrases.notes: Above and below refer to the red line that divided the upper and lower halves of the מזבח.

phrases.english: and those meant to be placed below, above
and those meant to be placed...
phrases.notes: The sentence stops in the middle here and picks up on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מְנָת לִיתְּנָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a new group of wrong plans, now about putting the blood in the wrong spot on the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The list of wrong-place plans begins here. The ruling for these cases comes after the list ends, on the next amud.
